title: BI International Baccalaureate Scholarship
duration: Up to three years of 100% tuition fees
description: The BI International Baccalaureate Scholarship is awarded to applicants who graduate with the top grades from the International Baccalaureate programme and covers 100% of tuition fees for up to three years provided the student maintains the academic progression requirements. Applicants need a minimum of 33 IB points, final or predicted, and an offer of admission to the Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Data Science for Business or Bachelor of Digital Business programme. title: Future African Leader Scholarship
funding: Fully Funded (full tuition up to two years plus a NOK 50,000 per semester living-expense stipend)
duration: Up to two years of full tuition fees plus a per-semester stipend
description: The Future African Leader Scholarship is one of two MSc scholarships BI offers to support its membership of the GBSN Network and GMAC's Study in Europe Initiative, specifically for candidates in Africa. Each award covers full tuition fees for up to two years plus a stipend for living expenses of NOK 50,000 per semester, conditional on meeting the academic progression requirements. Applicants must be international citizens who are not residents of Norway, hold a minimum overall GPA of 4.0 on the ECTS scale, submit strong GMAT or GRE scores, and be admitted to the first year of an MSc programme

title: NTNU PhD Positions (Salaried Employment)
funding: Fully Funded (salaried employment as a PhD research fellow / stipendiat)
official_source: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
duration: Three-year full-time study as standard; some positions include a fourth year of required duties, usually teaching, as detailed in the employee contract
description: NTNU's PhD positions are salaried employment rather than scholarships: Norwegian PhD candidates are not treated as students and are normally employees of the institution that funds them. Most PhD candidates at NTNU are employed as PhD research fellows (stipendiat) at NTNU or a university college, with individual positions advertised on NTNU's vacancy pages and on jobbnorge.no. Admission requires at least five years of higher education including a master's degree, a weighted average of at least B over the last two master's years on NTNU's scale, and a funding plan for the whole PhD period. title: NORPART – Norwegian Partnership Programme
official_source: Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir)
program_type: Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills institutional collaboration grant, not a student scholarship
duration: Funded projects under the 2024 call had to start between 1 November and 31 December 2024 and end by 31 December 2028; individual exchange stays are capped at 12 months (master) and 18 months (PhD).
description: NORPART, the Norwegian Partnership Programme for Global Academic Exchange, is an institutional scheme run by HK-dir that supports collaboration between Norwegian and partner-country higher education institutions. The applicant must be an accredited Norwegian higher education institution and the application must include an accredited partner institution in a NORPART partner country. title: Master Mind Scholarships — Flemish Government
official_source: Flemish Ministry of Education and Training / VLUHR
duration: One academic year for a 60 ECTS master's programme, or two academic years for a 120 ECTS master's programme. For a one-year programme, the final instalment of EUR 1,525 is not awarded if the master's degree is not obtained by July or September 2027. For a two-year programme, at least 54 ECTS must be obtained in the first academic year by July or September 2027 to receive the final instalment of EUR 1,525 of year one and to be entitled to the scholarship for the second year. Exceptions can only be granted by VLUHR in agreement with the hosting institution and the Department of Education and Training.
description: The applicant applies to take up a Master degree programme at a Flemish higher education institution (hereafter ‘Host institution’).

title: Inspiring the Outstanding Scholarship
official_source: KU Leuven (financed by the KU Leuven International Scholarship Fund)
description: KU Leuven's centrally funded master's scholarship, financed by donations to the KU Leuven International Scholarship Fund. For the 2026-2027 academic year one scholarship was available, awarded to an outstanding applicant to any eligible KU Leuven master's or advanced master's programme. Holders receive a full tuition fee waiver, pay only an annual administration fee of circa EUR 140, and receive an allowance of EUR 13,200 per academic year for a maximum of two academic years. title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Degrees (EMJMD/EMJM) Scholarships
duration: 1 to 2 academic years, typically 60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits
description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees are integrated international master's programmes jointly delivered by at least three higher education institutions from at least three different countries, at least two of which are EU Member States or Programme-associated third countries. The European Commission funds the programmes and offers EU scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide at EUR 1,400 per month for a maximum of 24 months. Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme, usually between October and January for entry the following academic year.
